audits.title: Better by half: hypertension in the elderly and the 'rule of halves': a primary care audit of the clinical computer record as a springboard to improving care.
audits.standard: 'Rule of halves' for hypertension; locally agreed guidelines and targets
audits.setting: West London general practices using EMIS computer system

cycle1.result: Using strict definitions the rule of halves still applied; using looser definitions three-quarters of hypertensives known, two-thirds treated and just under two-thirds controlled.

audits.intervention: Feedback of results to practices, agreed management guidelines, standardised computer recording, targets and review dates.
audits.other_findings: Wide variation in computer use, follow-up, target BP attainment and prescribing; 15 practices used computers regularly.
audits.citation: Hooker RC, Cowap N, Newson R, Freeman GK. Better by half: hypertension in the elderly and the 'rule of halves': a primary care audit of the clinical computer record as a springboard to improving care. Fam Pract. 1999;16(2):123-128. doi:10.1093/fampra/16.2.123. PMID: 10381016.

audits.title: A clinical audit of the quality of care of hypertension in general practice.
audits.standard: Ministry of Health Jamaica hypertension standards of care
audits.setting: Primary care practices of five family medicine residents

cycle1.result: Nutritional advice 33%; smoking/alcohol history 40%; physical activity 30%; fundoscopy 11%; foot examination 30%; yearly electrolytes 28%.

audits.intervention: Physicians sensitised to preliminary audit results.

cycle2.result: Nutritional advice 74%; smoking/alcohol 65%; physical activity 47%; fundoscopy 54%; foot exam 58%; electrolytes 62%.

audits.citation: Asnani M, Brown P, O'Connor D, Lewis T, Win S, Reid M. A clinical audit of the quality of care of hypertension in general practice. West Indian Med J. 2005;54(3):176-180. doi:10.1590/s0043-31442005000300004. PMID: 16209222.

audits.title: Audit of hypertension in general practice.
audits.standard: Structure, process and outcome indicators with targets (BP 140/90 or less, 130/80 with diabetes or renal insufficiency)

cycle1.result: Targets met for only four indicators (weight 89%, BP monitoring 85.8%, follow-up within 6 months 87.9%, mean diastolic BP 73.9%); 743 (59%) reached target BP.

audits.other_findings: Other indicators ranged 22.1% to 68.7%; wide variation between clinics.
audits.citation: Chan SC, Chandramani T, Chen TY, Chong KN, Harbaksh S, Lee TW, et al.. Audit of hypertension in general practice. Med J Malaysia. 2005;60(4):475-482. PMID: 16570710.

audits.title: An audit of hypertension at university health center in oman.
audits.standard: Recording of care items in a pre-designed structured form
audits.setting: Family Medicine Staff Clinic, Sultan Qaboos University

cycle1.result: Age, gender, blood pressure, renal function and lipids recorded in >75%; pertinent symptoms and smoking history poorly recorded.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documentation of pertinent symptoms.

audits.citation: Al-Shidhani TA, Bhargava K, Rizvi S. An audit of hypertension at university health center in oman. Oman Med J. 2011;26(4):248-252. doi:10.5001/omj.2011.60. PMID: 22043428.

audits.title: Improving the quality of care for patients with hypertension in Moshupa District, Botswana: quality improvement cycle.
audits.standard: Target standards for structure, process and outcome of hypertension care
audits.setting: Moshupa clinic and catchment area, Moshupa District

cycle1.result: None of the target standards met.

audits.intervention: Simple interventions designed and implemented to improve care (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Six of nine structural, five of 11 process and one of two outcome target standards achieved.

audits.other_findings: Significant improvement in blood pressure control was also seen.
audits.citation: Kande C, Mash R. Improving the quality of care for patients with hypertension in Moshupa District, Botswana: quality improvement cycle. Afr J Prim Health Care Fam Med. 2014;6(1):E1-4. doi:10.4102/phcfm.v6i1.578. PMID: 26245397.

audits.title: A longitudinal chart audit of hypertension in a family practice center.

cycle1.result: Diagnosis properly made in all patients and evaluation and therapy appropriate; family and past medical history poorly recorded.

audits.intervention: New history database sheet and chronic disease flow sheet designed.
audits.citation: Harris AE Jr, McDowell J, Schoen RG. A longitudinal chart audit of hypertension in a family practice center. J Fam Pract. 1977;5(6):939-945. PMID: 304095.

audits.title: An audit of hypertensive care in general practice.
audits.standard: WHO diagnostic criteria and standards of hypertension care
audits.setting: Mainly urban general practice, Bridge St Medical Centre, Derry

cycle1.result: Use of WHO criteria for diagnosis rose from 38.6% to 59% over five years; 78.9% had BP checked in the previous year; history taking and investigations suboptimal.

audits.other_findings: Practice prevalence of hypertension 5.31% (10.8% in those aged 30-80); hospitals involved in management of 53.9%.
audits.citation: Meagher PF, Deery C, Linton AF, Craig TJ, Leeson PJ. An audit of hypertensive care in general practice. Ir Med J. 1993;86(1):20-22. PMID: 8444586.

audits.title: Interpractice audit of diagnosis and management of hypertension in primary care: educational intervention and review of medical records.
audits.standard: At least three blood pressure readings before treatment; recording of BMI, lipids and urea and electrolytes; blood pressure control
audits.setting: Six general practices in north west London

cycle1.result: Pre-education levels of care not given in figures.

audits.intervention: Peer review audit with educational intervention.

cycle2.result: Improved recording of BMI, total lipids and urea and electrolytes; no improvement in diagnosis or blood pressure control.

audits.citation: Mashru M, Lant A. Interpractice audit of diagnosis and management of hypertension in primary care: educational intervention and review of medical records. BMJ. 1997;314(7085):942-946. doi:10.1136/bmj.314.7085.942. PMID: 9099120.

audits.title: A collaborative audit of the management of hypertension in general practice.
audits.standard: Standards based on current hypertension guidelines
audits.setting: 14 general practices, Portsmouth and South East Hampshire Health Authority

cycle1.result: Pretreatment BP measured on 3 or more occasions in 87%; BP measured in the preceding year in 90%; current BP <150/95 mmHg in 82.5% and <140/90 mmHg in 44%; thiazide first line in 30%.

audits.other_findings: Hypertension prevalence was 3.5%, lower than expected; beta-blockers were the most popular initial treatment.
audits.citation: Raman GV, Neal A, Lewis C. A collaborative audit of the management of hypertension in general practice. Postgrad Med J. 1998;74(869):165-167. doi:10.1136/pgmj.74.869.165. PMID: 9640443.

audits.title: Audit on hypertension management in general practice.

cycle1.result: Hypertension prevalence 9% of adults; adequate monitoring and follow-up in only one third of hypertensive patients.

audits.other_findings: Effect on subsequent practice performance discussed but not reported in abstract.
audits.citation: Neville RG, McKellican JF. Audit on hypertension management in general practice. Fam Pract. 1984;1(3):168-172. doi:10.1093/fampra/1.3.168. PMID: 6530079.
